issues.description: The method messageOnMilk() has conflicting return types between the problem statement and the reference solution. The UML in the problem statement (problem_statement.md, lines 51-53) declares Milkable.messageOnMilk(): boolean, and the textual requirement (problem_statement.md, lines 92-95) states "messageOnMilk() should return true if milking was successful, false otherwise." In the reference solution, the interface (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java) declares messageOnMilk() as returning String (signature at line 5), and the concrete classes Seal and Goat implement messageOnMilk() returning String (signatures at solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Seal.java line 19 and solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Goat.java line 15). This mismatch (boolean vs String) is a structural API contradiction that will confuse students about the expected method signature and will cause test/implementation incompatibilities.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the API consistent across all artifacts. Two valid remedies: (A) Update the problem statement (UML and textual description) to specify that Milkable.messageOnMilk() returns a String (and provide an example message), then update the task descriptions so students implement and test a String-returning messageOnMilk(). Also update template and tests accordingly. OR (B) Change the reference solution so Milkable.messageOnMilk() returns boolean, and modify Seal and Goat (and any tests/examples) to return true/false (and, if desired, print string messages elsewhere). After choosing one option, ensure the interface, all concrete classes, the template, the UML diagram, and the textual requirements are aligned.
